DTR
DEE-tee-AR
noun (Millennial slang)
Initialism for define the relationship, the conversation in which two people dating decide what they are to each other: exclusive or not, boyfriend and girlfriend or "just talking." The phrase is widely associated with 1990s evangelical college campuses, where the "DTR talk" was a rite of passage; it spread through 2000s dating culture, and became essential in the 2010s app era of situationships, "talking stages," and ambiguous hookups, when the default was to leave everything undefined.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A DTR is the conversation where a couple stops guessing and says out loud what they are to each other. The Millennial dating world needed a name for it because so much of that world was designed to avoid it: hanging out, talking, seeing where it goes, never saying. The Christian observation: the instinct behind the DTR is righteous and sorely needed. Scripture prizes clarity in relationships between men and women. The Lord Jesus said, "let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay" (Mat 5:37). Ruth asked Boaz plainly at the threshing floor, "spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman" (Rut 3:9), and Boaz answered just as plainly and acted the next morning. Rebekah was asked, "Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go" (Gen 24:58). Biblical courtship is a long DTR: a man declares his intention toward marriage, families are involved, and both know where they stand. What the Millennial DTR often lacks is a destination; it defines the relationship as "exclusive" without asking "toward what?" A father tells his son: if you are spending time alone with a girl, you owe her and her father a definition, and the honest one is "I am considering marriage." He tells his daughter: if a boy will not define it, he has defined it already.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial slang (1990s, associated with Christian colleges) for define the relationship; redeemable as the honest clarity Scripture prizes (Mat 5:37; Rut 3:9), best when the definition points toward marriage.

DTR, n. (Millennial dating slang, 1990s–present; initialism of define the relationship) The conversation in which a dating couple clarifies their status and intentions. "We had the DTR last night." Contrast situationship, "talking stage."

Decode for parents: if your child cannot say what a relationship is, it needs a DTR, and the best definition names marriage as the aim.

Key Scripture

Mat 5:37 — "But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil."

Rut 3:9 — "And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman."

Gen 24:58 — "And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go."

Pro 13:12 — "Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life."

1Th 4:6 — "That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified."

Modern Corruption

DTR rightly demands clarity in a dating culture built on ambiguity; its weakness is a definition with no destination, and Scripture’s definition points to covenant.

expand to see more

The need for the DTR exposes the disease of modern dating: deliberate ambiguity. Relationships drift for months without anyone saying what they are, which keeps options open for the one with less at stake and leaves the other in limbo. "Hope deferred maketh the heart sick" (Pro 13:12). The ambiguity is not neutral. Paul warns "That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter" (1Th 4:6), in a passage about sexual purity; to take the affection of someone while withholding a commitment is a kind of fraud.

The redemption is to make the definition early and honest, and to give it a direction. Christian courtship is not a series of DTRs, each one a little more exclusive, but a single declared purpose: I am pursuing you toward marriage, and I will do it openly. Teach the young that clarity is kindness, that the honest no is better than months of maybe, and that the best relationship definitions are spoken at last in vows.

"Ruth’s DTR at the threshing floor was plain, and Boaz answered by morning (Rut 3:9)."

"Hope deferred maketh the heart sick (Pro 13:12): define it."
